# Results — Study 956 (the ADR custody fee) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Fifteen ADR / home-line / FX
triples; the estimand is the slope in time of `log(ADR total return) − log(home line total
return × FX)`, reported as a positive annual cost. Daily closes via `yfinance`; the
**total-return** leg is `auto_adjust=True` and the **price-only** leg is `auto_adjust=False`
(Yahoo's split-adjusted `Close`) — both are labelled everywhere below. The regression
carries a separate intercept per detected level-shift segment, so an ADS-ratio change
contributes nothing to the slope. As-of **2026-06-30** (the partial current month is
dropped).*

## Data stamp

| Panel | Window | n rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR total-return panel (15 tickers) | 2000-01-03 → 2026-06-30 | 6,649 | `ccd87508f03e` |

Legs cached per name: `prices_<T>` (total return), `praw_<T>` (price only) for both the ADR
and the home line, plus six FX crosses (`EURUSD=X`, `CHF=X`, `DKK=X`, `JPY=X`, `TWD=X`,
`GBPUSD=X`) and `BIL` for the excess-of-cash leg.

## The coverage screen — and the trap it catches

The gate reads **only the home line's own realised distribution yield** (total-return close
minus price-only close), never the ADR's and never the gap between them, so it cannot
select for a small or a large answer.

| | Home yield | ADR yield | ADR / home | |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| TTE, SNY, SAP, PHG, ING, E, NVS, NVO, TM, TSM | 1.86 – 6.28 %/yr | 1.55 – 6.00 %/yr | 0.84 – 1.00 | **kept** |
| SHEL, BP, HSBC, UL, RIO (all LSE) | **0.04 – 0.05 %/yr** | 3.58 – 5.82 %/yr | **97 – 114 ×** | **dropped** |

*(Screen yields are endpoint-to-endpoint; the per-name table below reports the trend-fit
yields, which differ by a few basis points on the same series.)*

Yahoo's LSE "adjusted close" is **split-adjusted only** — the London home leg is missing its
entire dividend stream. Comparing it naively against the ADR manufactures a **−5.4 %/yr
"custody fee"**, roughly a hundred times any real depositary charge. Five of fifteen pairs,
a third of the intended sample, are unusable. **10 of 15 pairs survive.**

The **price placebo** is the same trend fit on the *price-only* ratio, which must be flat: an
ADS is a fixed number of shares. It is flat for six names and clearly is **not** for PHG
(+32.5 bp/yr), NVS (+23.2) and TSM (−30.6) — a slow drift in the ADR premium that
contaminates the *total*-drag column for those names. That is why the headline is the
**income gap**: it is measured from `log(TR) − log(price-only)` on each leg separately, so it
is free of both the price ratio and the FX cross (FX multiplies both closes of a leg
identically and cancels).

**Do not read the per-name HAC *t* column as strength.** An income series is a near
deterministic staircase — its regression residual is tiny — so a 252-lag HAC *t* on it is
wildly overconfident (NVO reports *t* = +12.10 on a gap of **1.5 bp/yr**). The honest
per-name inference is the block bootstrap two sections below, which clears zero on three
names, not ten. The columns are printed because the estimator prints them, and are
contradicted on purpose.

## The headline — pooled across names

| Quantity | mean | median | sd | *t* | positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Total drag | +16.71 bp/yr | +7.62 | 27.52 | +1.92 | 9/10 |
| Price placebo | +3.00 bp/yr | +0.57 | 16.51 | +0.58 | 8/10 |
| **Income gap** | **+13.80 bp/yr** | **+7.53** | 18.48 | **+2.36** | **9/10** |
| Income gap, cents per ADS | +9.01 c | +5.34 c | 12.77 | +2.23 | 9/10 |

- **Name-bootstrap 95 % CI** (resampling issuers, 5,000 draws): **[+4.96, +25.65] bp/yr**,
  equivalently **[+3.09, +17.57] cents per ADS per year**; share of draws ≤ 0 is **0.000**.
- **Sign test**: 9 of 10 names positive, exact one-sided *p* = **0.0107**.
- The published depositary schedules sit at **1–5 cents per ADS per year**. The tape's
  median, **5.3 cents**, lands on the top of that band; the mean, 9.0 cents, above it.
  A coincidence of magnitudes is not an attribution — see *What this number is not*, below.

**The cross-name *t* assumes ten independent issuers, and they are not.** Six of the ten
are euro-area names sharing a currency, a treaty rate and a dividend calendar. Collapse
each currency block to a single observation (EUR +8.69, CHF +59.30, DKK +1.55, JPY +11.87,
TWD +13.21 bp/yr) and the pooled *t* falls to **+1.84 on n = 5** — below the desk's bar.
The name bootstrap inherits the same optimism, since it resamples names, not blocks.

## Where it is fragile

- **Leave-one-out.** The cross-name mean ranges +8.75 → +15.43 bp/yr and the *t* ranges
  **+1.92 → +2.67**. Dropping **Eni** alone takes the *t* below 2; dropping **Novartis**
  (an 4× outlier, and the one name with both a 2019 Alcon and a 2023 Sandoz spin-off that the
  depositary and the home line record differently) halves the mean to +8.75 bp/yr. The
  headline *t* is knife-edge, not robust.
- **Per-name block bootstrap** (63-day blocks, 600 draws) is far less generous than the HAC
  *t*: only **3 of 10** names have a CI clear of zero (NVS [+19.3, +94.5], TSM [+8.7, +25.9],
  TM [+2.1, +49.0]); SAP is marginal (share ≤ 0 = 0.052) and the other six straddle zero.
  Name by name, the leak is invisible.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2015-01-01)

| Era | n names | Income gap | *t* | positive | Price placebo | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2000-01-03 → 2014-12-31 | 10 | **+19.99 bp/yr** | +2.65 | 10/10 | +13.48 | +1.11 |
| 2015-01-02 → 2026-06-30 | 10 | **+10.23 bp/yr** | +2.09 | 6/10 | +2.44 | +0.12 |

Positive in both halves, but roughly halving — consistent with depositary fee schedules
converging and with more names moving to fee-free structures, and equally consistent with
noise.

## The ASSUMPTION sweep — and why the fee/tax split fails

The **withholding rate is the only non-tape input** (treaty rates: 15 % France, Germany,
Netherlands, Italy, Switzerland, Denmark; 15.315 % Japan; 21 % Taiwan; 0 % UK). Scaling it:

| Assumed rate | Residual "custody" | *t* | names positive |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 × treaty (credit nothing to tax) | **+13.80 bp/yr** | +2.36 | 90 % |
| 0.5 × treaty | −14.67 bp/yr | −2.54 | 10 % |
| 1.0 × treaty | −43.15 bp/yr | −5.50 | 0 % |
| 1.5 × treaty (≈ statutory) | −71.62 bp/yr | −6.58 | 0 % |

At the treaty rates the withholding alone would cost **26–96 bp/yr** on these yields (SAP
25.9, NVO 30.4, TM 37.7, PHG 43.1, ING 49.3, SNY 59.9, NVS 62.9, TSM 77.1, TTE 87.2, E
96.0) — two to seven times the *entire* measured gap. The residual "custody fee" is
therefore **negative for every name**, which is not a finding about fees: it is proof that
the ADR total-return series **does not embed the withholding at all**. Yahoo's per-ADS
dividend is evidently the gross declared amount. Only the 0.0 × column is a defensible
reading of this tape.

The identification plan had a fallback and it also failed. The five **UK** pairs would have
pinned the split — the UK levies no dividend withholding tax, so for them the income gap
*is* the custody fee by law — but they are precisely the five London listings the coverage
screen destroys. Nothing in the surviving panel identifies the split.

### What this number is not

Follow the last argument one step further. If the vendor records the **gross declared**
per-ADS dividend, then whatever the depositary announces is what lands in the series — and
the depositary fee, when it is billed as a separate DTC / broker line item rather than
netted out of the announced rate (which is how a large share of the schedule is actually
collected), never touches this tape either. The measured **+13.80 bp/yr is therefore an
unattributed income residual**: an upper bound on the custody fee, consistent with the
published 1–5 cent schedule but not evidence for it, and equally consistent with the
depositary's FX-conversion spread on the dividend, with rounding of the per-ADS rate, and
with residual differences in how the vendor's two feeds (the ADR's and the home line's)
record special dividends and spin-offs. Novartis (+59.3 bp/yr, four times the pooled mean, two spin-offs) is the visible
face of that last one. **This study measures a leak. It does not name it.**

## Break-threshold sweep (level-shift detector)

| Threshold | Total drag | *t* | Price placebo | mean segments |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.06 | +20.11 bp/yr | +2.56 | +6.48 | 1.20 |
| 0.10 (headline) | +16.71 bp/yr | +1.92 | +3.00 | 1.10 |
| 0.15 | +16.71 bp/yr | +1.92 | +3.00 | 1.10 |
| 0.25 | +16.71 bp/yr | +1.92 | +3.00 | 1.10 |

Exactly **one** break is found across the ten kept names — ING on **2009-11-23**, the
state-aid rights issue — which is why ING is the only name showing two segments and why
the answer is flat from a 0.10 threshold upward. Among the *dropped* UK names the detector
also flags Shell's 2005 unification and the 2009 HSBC and Rio Tinto rights issues, i.e.
exactly the corporate events it is for.

## The only traded leg — own the home line instead of the ADR

Equal-weight ADR basket versus the same basket bought on its home markets, both
**excess-of-cash** (minus BIL's total return), long only so no borrow, one-way FX conversion
× NAV executed at **t + 1** on a signal formed at *t*. 4,071 common days (BIL's 2007
inception gates the cash leg). Both friction inputs are **ASSUMPTIONS** and both are swept.

| FX conversion | Foreign custody | ADR Sharpe | Home Sharpe | advantage | ann. diff | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bp (gross) | 0 bp/yr | +0.547 | +0.608 | +0.061 | **+14.6 bp** | **+0.11** |
| 30 bp | 0 bp/yr | +0.547 | +0.607 | +0.060 | +12.8 bp | +0.10 |
| 30 bp | 15 bp/yr | +0.547 | +0.600 | +0.054 | **−2.2 bp** | −0.02 |
| 50 bp | 30 bp/yr | +0.547 | +0.593 | +0.046 | −18.5 bp | −0.14 |

Gross, the home basket beats the ADR basket by **+14.6 bp/yr at HAC *t* = +0.11** — the
leak is a rounding error next to the 20 %-a-year volatility it is buried in. A **15 bp/yr**
foreign safekeeping charge, well inside what a US brokerage charges for foreign settlement,
erases it outright.

Two reasons this leg is a *measurement*, not a backtest anyone could have run:

- **It inherits look-ahead.** The frames arrive through a bad-print screen whose rolling
  median is **centred**, so it peeks a few days forward. On the headline that is inert —
  the pooled income gap is **+13.80 bp/yr with the filter on and +13.80 with it off**,
  because a trend fit on a level cannot be moved by isolated bad prints. On *this* leg it
  is decisive: switching the filter off takes the same race to **+944.7 bp/yr at HAC
  *t* = +1.05**, since **24 rows out of 83,728** (0.03 % — corrupt closes in `TWD=X` and
  `NOVO-B.CO`) dominate an arithmetic mean of daily returns. The cleaned number is the
  right one, but it is produced with information a live trader would not have had. Both
  readings are Mirage.
- **Rebalancing turnover is charged on neither leg** — only the single entry conversion. A
  genuinely daily-rebalanced home-market basket pays FX on every trade and the ADR basket
  does not, so the home leg's gross advantage above is an upper bound on itself.

## Synthetic control (machinery proof only — never supports the stamp)

| World | Planted (exact gap) | Recovered income gap | Residual custody | Price placebo |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Fee 25.0 + tax 52.5 bp/yr | 76.31 bp/yr | **+76.31** (*t* = +106) | +24.33 (planted 25.0) | +1.12 |
| No fee, no tax | 0.00 bp/yr | **+0.11** (*t* = +0.12) | +0.11 | +1.12 |
| Null × 8 seeds | 0.00 bp/yr | mean **−0.28**, sd 1.69 | — | — |
| Fee + tax + a 0.70-log ADS-ratio step | 76.31 bp/yr | +74.51 (total drag) | — | — |

*(The planted gap is 76.31 rather than the nominal 25.0 + 52.5 = 77.5 because the two legs
compound their per-payment yields; the estimator is asked to recover the exact figure.)*

The estimator recovers a planted fee to within a basis point, splits it correctly when the
withholding rate is *known*, is silent on the null on 0 of 8 seeds, and is unmoved by a
planted ADS-ratio change. The real-tape ambiguity is a property of the tape, not the harness.

## Verdict

- **Signal — Weak.** The ADR really does hand its holder less income than the home line:
  **+13.80 bp/yr** pooled (median +7.53), positive on **9 of 10** names (sign test
  *p* = 0.011), name-bootstrap CI **[+4.96, +25.65] bp/yr** clear of zero, positive in both
  eras, and a median of **5.3 cents per ADS per year** that sits on the published 1–5 cent
  schedules. It does not clear a *robust* bar, on five separate counts: the pooled *t* is
  **+2.36**, falls to **+1.92** on leave-one-out and to **+1.84** when the six euro-area
  issuers are collapsed into the one observation they really are; only **3 of 10** names
  have a block-bootstrap CI clear of zero; the mean is inflated by Novartis, a 4× outlier
  with two spin-offs the two feeds record differently (drop it: **+8.75 bp/yr**); the price
  placebo is contaminated on three names; and **a third of the intended sample is unusable**
  because the vendor's LSE adjusted close carries no dividends. The panel is a **survivor
  panel** of issuers still listed on both venues in 2026, which excludes the de-sponsored
  ADRs where fee disputes concentrate.
- **And the fee itself is not identified.** The assumed withholding (26–96 bp/yr) exceeds
  the whole measured gap, so the tax is demonstrably absent from the tape; the same
  argument means a fee billed as a separate DTC line item would be absent too. **+13.80
  bp/yr is an unattributed income residual and an upper bound on the depositary fee, not a
  measurement of it.** The UK names that would have pinned the split are exactly the five
  the coverage screen destroys.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** Nothing to bank. Owning the home lines instead beats the ADRs by
  **+14.6 bp/yr gross at HAC *t* = +0.11**, and a 15 bp/yr foreign safekeeping charge — less
  than any US brokerage's foreign settlement cost — flips it negative. Rebalancing turnover
  is charged on neither leg, and the leg inherits a forward-peeking bad-print filter without
  which it reads +944.7 bp/yr at *t* = +1.05. It is a measurement of a small unavoidable
  wrapper cost, not an arbitrage, under either reading.
- **What a holder should take from it.** Budget roughly **5–10 cents per ADS per year** of
  invisible wrapper cost, or about 10 bp on a typical $50–100 ADS, plus whatever your
  custodian's own foreign-dividend handling costs. It is small, it is invisible on a price
  chart, it cannot be decomposed from public data, and it is not worth crossing a border to
  escape.
